description: Dead-man for the frame-differencing visual monitor (sensor.camera_visual_activity). Added 2026-08-30. Until now this was the ONLY monitor of the four with no dead-man, no derived binary_sensor and no availability guard - grep for camera_visual_activity across all 35 automations returned zero. That mattered because its most likely failure is not a crash but going BLIND while still running: cam_vision.py rewrites its state file every cycle regardless, and cam_motion.py used that file's mtime as its only freshness gate, so a camera nobody could actually see read as a camera that was quiet - the reassuring branch. The one signal that might have caught the monitor stopping (cam_flap's probe_shortfall) was calibrated for a single prober while two sensors probed the same endpoints, so cam_vision dying merely halved the probe stream to a level still above the bar; since 2026-10-14 cam_vision analyses cam_health's shared frames instead of probing, so its death does not show in the probe counts at all. Fires on death OR on any camera going unseen for 15+ min; re-asserts hourly (:29) as a restart-wipe guard. (2026-10-10: the unavailable/unknown hold is an OR of single-state conditions with for:, because HA 2026.10 rejects for: with a list of states.) 2026-10-28: START-UP CHECK. A state trigger needs a change after it attaches, so a monitor that was already dead when Home Assistant started (a Core update, or a deploy followed by a restart, that breaks the script) never fired this alert, and the re-assert restores the card without a push. On the start trigger the run now waits up to 30 min for the monitor to be healthy and pages if it is not; its push says the fault has been present since the start, because the check repeats, once per start, a page sent before the restart. The check runs only on a Home Assistant start: an automation reload that re-arms the triggers while the fault is present is not covered. The boot trigger this alert already had could never pass: its conditions required the binary, or the sensor's dead state, to have held for 30 min, and last_changed resets at every start. After an outage of 15 min or more every camera is unseen at the start; that clears on the first vision run after the engine serves frames again, inside the wait. camera_monitor_stalled pushes an unchanging error or an unknown state about 60 min after the start; this check pushes at 30.

then.stop: the monitor was healthy at the start or recovered within the hold

data.message: The frame-differencing visual monitor has been degraded for 30+ min (state: {{ states('sensor.camera_visual_activity') }}). While it is down, every per-camera staleness verdict falls back to "no verdict" rather than silently reading as a quiet area - that guard is deliberate. Summary: {{ state_attr('sensor.camera_visual_activity','summary') or 'attributes wiped' }}. Cameras not seen: {{ state_attr('sensor.camera_visual_activity','blind') or 'n/a' }}. Cross-camera corroboration in cam_motion.py is unaffected and still works. {{ now().strftime('%b %-d %-I:%M %p') }}.
